The code name of India's first nuclear weapon test, an underground explosion at the army's Pokhran range in the Rajasthan desert on 18 May 1974.

India's nuclear programme went back to Homi Bhabha in the 1940s. The war with China in 1962 and China's own bomb test in 1964 pushed India toward a weapon. The device was built under the government of Indira Gandhi by a small team led by the physicist Raja Ramanna. The plutonium came from a research reactor that Canada had supplied for peaceful use. The test was set for Buddha Purnima, the Buddha's birthday, hence the code name.

India called it a "peaceful nuclear explosion" and did not build up an arsenal openly for years. But the test made India the first country outside the five permanent members of the UN Security Council to explode a bomb by its own effort. Its effects were wide. Canada cut nuclear help, and the main supplier states formed the Nuclear Suppliers Group to control exports. Pakistan sped up its own programme. In 1998 India tested again at Pokhran, and Pakistan answered within weeks. The science behind it began with nuclear fission.
sum: The code name of India's first nuclear weapon test, an underground explosion at the army's Pokhran range in the Rajasthan desert on 18 May 1974.
